text:
emma: FYI I'm bringing up customer 'Lyra' LoRA v2 on the int8 runtime this morning. Focused quick-eval uses their invoice pack + a tiny conversational set.

dan: great. last time their tokenizer had merged punctuation tokens which shifted amounts. did you run a token delta?

emma: ran token-delta compare and applied a remap. cmd:
```
python infra/token_delta.py --base models/base-lyra/tokenizer.json --target customers/lyra/tokenizer.json --emit remap/lyra_delta.json
```

ci-bot: queued: quick-eval/1733333333-lyra-int8-invoice-check (priority: medium)

kevin: quick peek at generated totals looks mostly ok, but one prompt showed decimal truncation (21.499 -> 21.4). could be rounding after quantized logits.

priya: customer requires cent-level accuracy. If rounding errors persist we might keep their invoice route on fp16.

emma: initial quant config (from recommendations):
```
quant_mode: int8
per_channel: true
group_size: 64
clip_value: 6.0
kv_prefill: true
```
I'm going to try disabling kv_prefill and toggling per_channel=false to see impact.

ci-bot: quick-eval started -> quick-eval/1733333333-lyra-int8-invoice-check: 0/30 complete

emma: running eval script:
```
python tools/run_quick_eval.py --model base-lyra --lora customers/lyra/lyra-lora-v2 --quant int8 --prompts eval_packs/lyra_invoices_small.json --out /tmp/lyra_eval.json --batch 2
```

emma: mid-run notes: 15/30 done. saw two cases where cents truncated and one case where trailing zero dropped ("$5.00" -> "$5.0"). Noticed p95 latency down 20% but p99 unchanged.

dan: truncation could be from post-processing normalization in our extractor. can you dump raw token ids for failing cases?

emma: dumped tokenids and decoded tokens for sample #8:
```
input: "Items: $12.99, $3.50. Total?"
raw_ids: [101, 22, 305, 999, 77, 3001, 305, 21]
decoded: ["Items", ":", "$12", ".99", ",", "$3", ".50", "Total?"]
```
root cause seems to be tokenizer splitting $12.99 into "$12" and ".99" vs expected "$12.99". That discrepancy came from customer's tokenizer remap.

kevin: ah, so it's upstream tokenization mismatch not quant per se. We should prefer the customer's tokenizer during inference, or stitch tokens back in postprocess.

priya: which option is faster to ship? customer wants a fix before next Monday.

emma: fastest: apply a small postprocess step that merges adjacent currency subtokens when pattern matches, add unit test for "$<digits>.<2digits>" sequences. I'll prototype and run full eval.

dan: add a regression test and include the tokenid diffs in the rollout notes so it's visible for future merges.

ci-bot: quick-eval complete: 30/30. summary: 27 pass, 3 tokenizer-related amount formatting regressions. artifacts: /ci/artifacts/quick-eval/1733333333/summary.json

emma: summary: no sign flips, no negative totals, failures due to token split/merge differences. Plan: 1) implement tokenizer-aware postprocess merge + unit test; 2) re-run quick-eval; 3) if green, create canary (5% traffic) keeping fp16 fallback on invoice endpoints until next major release.

kevin: SGTM. Also note we should add a lint rule in tokenization checks to catch currency splits for customer tokenizers.

priya: I'll prep the CS note and confirm timeline with Lyra. Please attach failing samples and patch when ready.

emma: opening infra/rollouts/1733333333 with artifacts and a PR link. tagging @priya for customer comms. Closing thread after PR lands.
